Anya: FYI — I pushed a compact variant of the Private/VPC setup network step to the Figma proto. Need a quick design + accessibility pass before we roll to QA. preview: https://figma.com/s/compact-net-step Mike: Looking now. Main thing for eng is reducing vertical space while keeping all validation visible. Can we keep one-line helper text under each field instead of the big paragraph? Jin: Agreed. Suggestion: hide the long primer behind a 'Network primer' collapsible, show a short 1-line summary near the header. Users who need details can expand. Sam: Accessibility note — collapsible must be keyboard-focusable and expose aria-expanded. Also ensure errors are programmatically describable via aria-describedby. Alex: On copy: replace 'Make sure your CIDR routes are open' with 'Confirm CIDR and routing to Redwood control plane (see primer)' — more actionable and links to KB. Anya: Good call. Also want inline tooltips for each prereq with a short example (e.g., sample CIDR, SSH port) that appears on focus/hover. Jin, can we do small (i) icons instead of full paragraphs? Jin: Yes. Proposed microcopy for tooltip: "Example: 10.0.0.0/16 — used for nodes. Ensure control-plane egress on 443." Tooltip should dismiss on blur. Mike: Implementation notes: tooltips need to be accessible and non-blocking for screen readers. We can use role=tooltip and aria-describedby on the input. Also prefer using the native focus outline — don't remove it in compact layout. Sam: Example ARIA pattern we should use: ```
Example: 10.0.0.0/16
``` This makes the help and error both discoverable. Anya: Nice. What about inline validation flow? Right now the proto validates on blur; we discussed validating on submit for noisy fields. Thoughts? Jin: For network fields — validate on blur for format (CIDR syntax/hostname) but run preflight (reachability) async after submit or when user clicks "Run preflight". Show a faint spinner next to the field while async checks run. Mike: Backend will expose an endpoint for preflight check per-field and a full-run. For UX, prefer a small status chip: pending -> success/fail. Keep statuses persistent in the UI so users can act on failing items. Alex: Copy for failure state suggestion: "Preflight failed: no route to control plane from 10.0.5.0/24. Try opening outbound 443 to or run connectivity diag." Short, includes next step. Anya: Love it. One more: compact layout keyboard flow. Jin, can you verify tab order in the proto? We should avoid jumps when chips appear. Jin: Will verify. Plan: always reserve space for the status chip (empty placeholder) so layout doesn't shift when it updates. preview-bot: Uploaded preview image — https://img.redwood.ai/previews/1768509999-compact-net.png Sam: Quick a11y check on preview: contrast of helper text in compact mode looks low at small sizes — bump to 3:1 at least for 12px helper. Mike: We'll update CSS vars and leave tokens for spacing. Also will keep the 24px touch target on the (i) icon for mobile. Anya: Next steps: Jin to update proto with collapsible primer + reserved chip spacing; Sam to run quick a11y test and list any color/token updates; Mike to wire the ARIA attributes and endpoint hooks; Alex to finish copy snippets for tooltips/errors. I'll sync with QA about a focused test plan. Aim to ship to staging by end of week. :thumbsup:
